timeline.body:
rewrites checkpointing as internal actions, reducing several sub-calls to
only 1 per data node that has at least 1 primary shard of the indexes of
interest.

Notes

Robustness: The current checkpointing sends a request to every shard - primary and replica - and collects the results. If 1 request fails, even for a replica, checkpointing fails. See #75780 for details.

Performance: The current checkpointing is wasteful, it uses get index and get index stats which results in a lot more calls and executes a lot more code which produces results we are not interested in.

### Number of node<->node messages:

old: `1 + shards * indices * (replicas + 1)`
new: `data_nodes`
(super precise: all data nodes with at least 1 primary shard of the requested indices)

e.g.

|shards|replicas|indices|data_nodes|old|new|
| ------: | --------: | -------: | ------: | ---: | ----: |
|1|1|1|1|4|1|
|5|1|1|1|11|1|
|5|1|5|3|51|3|
|5|1|20|8|201|8|
|5|1|100|10|1001|10|

Fixes #75780

This does not work because `GetCheckpointAction` is a cluster action (`cluster:admin/transform/checkpoint`). Authorization does not expand indices for cluster actions, this means the expansion here does not respect user's index access and could expand to anything that the cluster has. The quick fix is likely changing the action from `cluster:...` to `indices:...`.

reply.body:
Is my understanding correct?

If security is enabled it will resolve indices for me. However if security is disabled I need to resolve the indices myself this way. So either way I need this call. What strikes me: There seems no shortcut optimization, but it goes through a complex chain of code _again_ even if security already resolved it for me. But this might be another story and probably should be fixed in a separate PR.

Nit: The naming is quite poor, `IndicesRequest.Replaceable`, `indices(...)`: it is quite a lot of magic here and no indication that the implementation of it is mandatory.

timeline.body: The action needs to go through index expansion in the Authorization code. Otherwise, it does not respect user's access.
This request also needs to implement `IndicesRequest.Replaceable` so the indices are expandable for Authorization.
Thank you @ywangd for your help. I further investigated and implemented what we discussed. It would be nice if you can take a look again and provide your feedback.

`indices:internal/transform/checkpoint` is indexAction in that the request needs index name expansion. This means it cannot be part of a cluster privilege. It really needs be granted as an index privilege. I noticed you already add it as part of `view_index_metadata` index privilege. So I suggest we remove it from here.

For `cluster:internal/transform/*`, I don't know how transform works, so maybe this is normal: But having it here means the end-user needs to have both `manage_transform` cluster privilege and `view_index_metadata` index privilege for the actions to work. Is this expected?

reply.body:
> the end-user needs to have both manage_transform cluster privilege and view_index_metadata index privilege for the actions to work. Is this expected?

Yes, that's expected. The 2 actions are a replacement for the already existing checkpointing. It currently uses the index stats API's which require `view_index_metadata` ([documented](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/master/put-transform.html)). Note: the old implementation must be kept in order to provide backwards compatibility(e.g. for CCS).

Having that said, I would not mind if we find a solution that does not require `view_index_metadata`. At least in the long run.

timeline.body: `IndicesRequest.Replaceable` has a default method `boolean allowsRemoteIndices()` that returns `false`, which means the `indices` field cannot contain remote index names of the format `cluster_alias:index`. My reading of the code seems to suggest that all indices here have their cluster_alias prefix stripped (if any). So it should be OK for the class to rely on the default implementation of `allowsRemoteIndices()`. But it would be great if you could confirm on this.

reply.body: yes, that's correct. CCS is handled before calling this action: the `source` (indices to query) is split per cluster, get checkpoint is called separately for every cluster. This has been implemented like this for the original checkpointing, which as explained above is kept for BWC. It would be quite complex to separate the 2. Once the old style checkpointing got removed somewhen in future, we might revisit.

timeline.body:
I find it weird that this action is a clusterAction but the request still target indices (shards). I really think this should be an indexAction as well in the format of `indices:internal/transform/checkpoint[n]`. An example in the existing code and also similar to the scenario here is the FieldCaps request which is an indicesRequest:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2982591e6d8ee20fa5d7d78da1d0b456bbe056a4/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/fieldcaps/FieldCapabilitiesNodeRequest.java#L27

and the action name is `indices:data/read/field_caps[n]`:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2982591e6d8ee20fa5d7d78da1d0b456bbe056a4/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/fieldcaps/TransportFieldCapabilitiesAction.java#L52

Renaming it to be `indices:internal/transform/checkpoint[n]` also means it will be covered by the same `view_index_metadata` index privilege. So I suggest we rename the action to `indices:...` and make the associated request implements `IndicesRequest`.

reply.body: I stumbled upon the same thing. With `IndicesRequest` we carry the index names which is actually not necessary after resolving the shards, that's the reason why I kept it a cluster action. However it probably doesn't matter to send a few bytes more.

timeline.body:
Thanks Hendrik. I have some more suggestions/questions on how privilege works. 

Btw, if I understand the code correctly, the two new actions are trying to do something identical or at least similar to [`GetGlobalCheckpointsAction`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2982591e6d8ee20fa5d7d78da1d0b456bbe056a4/x-pack/plugin/fleet/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/fleet/action/GetGlobalCheckpointsAction.java#L49-L52). This action is in the fleet plugin and not exposed to other plugins. So not easily usable in Transform. The distributed didn't want to expose it more widely when it was first introduced and kinda considered it as beta. But it [does not seem to have any beta label](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.17/get-global-checkpoints.html). So maybe it's an useful thing to expose and resuse it today. A potential defficiency is that the GetGlobalCheckPoint API issues child request per shard which is less efficient than grouping them per node especially when the cluster size is large.

> Btw, if I understand the code correctly, the two new actions are trying to do something identical or at least similar to [`GetGlobalCheckpointsAction`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2982591e6d8ee20fa5d7d78da1d0b456bbe056a4/x-pack/plugin/fleet/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/fleet/action/GetGlobalCheckpointsAction.java#L49-L52). This action is in the fleet plugin and not exposed to other plugins. So not easily usable in Transform.

We considered this action and we would have taken the code and moved it around to make it usable. However it did not meet our requirements and the changes would have been quite large. This would neither help us nor fleet. You find more information and the discussion about using the fleet API in the corresponding [issue](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/75780).

@hendrikmuhs I think there really is just a single issue. So I'll comment here instead of under each comment for easy consumption.

The issue is: Cluster privilege should not be used to authorize indices actions with actual indices. Concretely for this PR, that means `manage_transform` should not be used for the `GetCheckpointNodeAction`. 

I am aware that you gave this action a name begins with `cluster:...`. But I don't think the name should decide whether the action is cluster or indices. In my opinion, it is the opposite, i.e. the nature of the action decides what name it should have. Since `GetCheckpointNodeAction` carries indices that must be authorized for the user, it is an Indices request and we should name it as such. Although these indices are already authorized in the parent request, it is still much safer to let the child requests run through the index authorization process again* as long as they still carry indices. It is a risky path to conditionally skipping it. Also index authorization needs to run (for both parent and child requests) for things like document level security (DLS) to work. Even though this particular use case does not concern DLS, proactively avoiding index authorization is riksy because too much knowledge is assumed by the caller.

In summary, I strongly recommend that we do something similar to `FieldCapabilitiesRequest` and `FieldCapabilitiesNodeRequest` for the privilege and authorization part. I am happy to jump on a sync if it helps.

> We considered this action and we would have taken the code and moved it around to make it usable. However it did not meet our requirements and the changes would have been quite large. This would neither help us nor fleet.

Sorry I wasn't aware that there were already previous discussions. Thanks for the pointer.

\* Index authorization has been improved a lot since 7.15. A child request with all concrete index names should not incur obvious overhead for authorization.

timeline.body:
@ywangd 

I have changed the implementation, so both actions are index actions now, the node action now carries indices and gets re-authorized. As you suggested I removed both actions from `manage_transform`. That means they are both fall under `view_index_metadata` now.

~FWIW: What confused me: the node action is not part of `view_index_metadata`, but nevertheless this works as the system integration tests indicate. Is it because I use the transport to call it?~
It works because of the wildcard: `GetCheckpointAction.NAME + "*"`.

timeline.author: Hendrik Muhs

timeline.body:
LGTM

@hendrikmuhs I appreciate your effort on the iterations and reaching out to us for awareness. Thanks a lot!

> It works because of the wildcard: GetCheckpointAction.NAME + "*"

Yes we intentionally use the suffix wildcard pattern so that privileges of child actions are also granted along with the parent action (assuming child actions are named using the suffix pattern).
